title: Junta Fourier coefficient estimate
statement: Let $n$ and $k$ be nonnegative integers, let $P$ be a set of coordinates in $	ext{Fin }n$, and let the failure parameter be rational and lie in $(0,1/2]$. Given a batch of restricted examples and a member $S$ of the low-degree junta Fourier family, the coefficient estimate is the empirical Fourier coefficient at $S$ computed from the coefficient sample sequence for that batch and $S$; it is rational-valued.
hypotheses_covered: $P$ is a finite set of coordinates in $	ext{Fin }n$
The failure parameter is rational and lies in $(0,1/2]$
The batch is a function on the indices up to the restricted sample count, with each value an assignment on coordinates outside $P$ paired with a sign
$S$ belongs to the low-degree junta Fourier family
